_comment: DreamRehearse real-robot rollouts. Source: HF repo hchen657Naza/real_world_videos, 4K/1080p camcorder takes staged on the node at <capture-path>/raw. Each web clip is a real-time trim of a single raw take (no speed change, no letterboxing). Raw clip id and source in/out timestamps per cell: hammer_ours=C0370 06.0-25.0s; hammer_base=C0355 12.0-31.0s; pour_ours=C0106 08.0-32.0s; pour_base=C0104 08.0-31.0s; tongs_ours=C0416 14.0-42.0s; tongs_base=C0417 10.0-33.0s; ood_vision_ours_1=C0089 13.0-35.0s; ood_vision_ours_2=C0092 12.0-35.0s; ood_vision_ours_3=C0095 18.0-40.3s; ood_vision_base_1=C0096 13.0-32.1s; ood_vision_base_2=C0097 09.0-30.7s. Hammer and tongs takes are 3840x2160@29.97 sources; pour and OOD takes are 1920x1080@50 sources; all are 16:9 and scale to 1280x720 with no padding. Encode: ffmpeg libx264 preset slow CRF 23, yuv420p, high profile, +faststart, -an (no audio), source frame rate preserved. Every outcome field below is a per-clip judgement made by inspecting frames of that take, not inferred from the directory name; see the pour row for a deliberate 'unclear'. Note: pour_base was re-cut from C0102 to C0104 because C0102 never lifts the bottle; C0104 completes the full pour gesture. Every base pour take was staged with an EMPTY bottle, so pour transfer is not assessable on the base side.

comparison.label: Hammer
comparison.caption: The robot picks up a rubber mallet and strikes the button on the red block.

comparison.label: Pour
comparison.caption: The robot picks up a bottle of candies and tips it over the yellow bowl to pour them in.

ours.note: Pour motion completed; one candy enters the bowl, then bounces out. Bulk stays in the bottle.

base.note: Pour motion completed; bottle was staged empty, so transfer is not assessable.

comparison.label: Tongs
comparison.caption: The robot picks up a pair of kitchen tongs, grips a small red cube with them, and places it on the blue plate.

robustness.label: Tablecloth and clutter
robustness.caption: The same hammer-the-button task, but staged on a white tablecloth and surrounded by kitchen clutter (a pan, stacked cups, plates, bread and utensils) in a rearranged layout.

failure_clips.note: Ours. Grasps the mallet handle cleanly and carries it to the red block, but the head tracks too high and passes to the left of the button without ever pressing it; the button cap is still proud at the end of the take.

Ours. Picks up the tongs and closes them on the red cube, but the cube is not retained during the lift; the tongs are set down on the blue plate empty and the plate is still empty at the end of the take.

Ours. Picks up the tongs and grips the red cube, then loses it in transit and drops it on the bare table just short of the plate; the tongs end up resting on the plate with the cube beside it, off the plate.

policies.ours: ACT trained on 5 real demonstrations plus 40 world-model dream demonstrations. For the robustness row it additionally saw out-of-distribution dreams (a white tablecloth and a different cluttered object layout).
policies.base: ACT trained on the same 5 real demonstrations only, with no dream data. For the robustness row it saw no OOD dreams.

meta.encode: H.264 (libx264, preset slow, CRF 23), yuv420p, high profile, +faststart, no audio. Scaled to 720p on the long edge preserving the source 16:9 aspect ratio (1280x720), source frame rate and real-time playback speed preserved; each clip is a straight trim of one raw take.
meta._score_note: comparison[].score is the real+dream student over 20 trials with the real-only baseline beside it, from the paper's real-robot table. It labels the task, not the individual clip shown: each clip is ONE rollout and carries its own outcome badge.
